strands.experiences: The learner is guided individually or in groups to:  use digital devices to watch video clips on frisbee games and observe the application of the rules.  Give each other feedback on the application of rules during a game session.  discuss the safety measures to be observed when playing games
strands.inquiryQuestions: How does frisbee assist in staying healthy?

strands.outcomes: By the end of the Sub Strand, the learner should be able to: a) perform the elbow stand for skill development b) observe precautions when performing the elbow stand for self and others safety. c) appreciate the elbow stand for balance
strands.experiences: The learner is guided individually, in pairs or in groups to:  use pictures and photographs observe the hand placement in the elbow stand  demonstrate the elbow stand and get feedback from the teacher.  practise the elbow- stand and give each other feedback.
strands.inquiryQuestions: Which fitness components are enhanced when performing the elbow stand?

strands.subStrand: Rolls: Dive forward roll into squat stand 2 Lessons
strands.outcomes: By the end of the Sub Strand, the learner should be able to: a) perform dive forward roll into squat stand for skill development. b) observe precautions when performing the Dive forward roll into squat stand for self and others safety.
strands.experiences: The learner is guided individually, in pairs or in groups to:  use digital devices to watch video clips of the dive forward roll into squat stand.  demonstrate the dive forward roll into squat stand and get feedback from the teacher.  practise the dive forward roll into squat stand and give each other feedback.
strands.inquiryQuestions: How can you ensure safe landing as you perform a dive forward roll?

strands.outcomes: By the end of the Sub Strand, the learner should be able to: a) perform the fence vault for skill development. b) observe precautions when performing the Fence vault for self and others safety.
strands.experiences: The learner is guided individually, in pairs or in groups to:  observe photographs and pictures of watch a video clip on performance of fence vault.  Demonstrate the fence vault and get feedback from the teacher  practise transferring body weight over obstacles of different heights.  take videos of each other and assess each other’s performance.
strands.inquiryQuestions: Which locally available objects can be used safely during vaulting?

strands.outcomes: By the end of the Sub Strand, the learners should be able to: a) perform two and three partner balances for skill development b) create two and three partner balances to enhance creativity and innovation. c) display two and three partner balances partner balances to enhance self- efficacy and for aesthetics. d) observe precautions when performing two and three partner balances for self and others safety.
strands.experiences: The learner is guided individually, in paors or in groups to:  use digital devices to watch video clips on two and three partner balances  demonstrate two and three partner balances and get feedback from the teacher  create two and three partner balances and display to school mates  discuss the safety measures to observe when performing two and three partner balances  take video clips of partner balances and display
strands.inquiryQuestions: Where can you display partner balances?

strands.outcomes: By the end of the Sub Strand, the learners should be able to: a) design a six-action sequence in gymnastics to enhance Critical thinking and problem solving a) display a six-action sequence for self-efficacy b) observe precautions when performing observe precautions when performing a two and three partner balances for own and others safety.
strands.experiences: The learner is guided individually, in pairs or in groups to:  discuss a six-action sequence and write down.  demonstrate the performance of two and three partner balances and get feedback from the teacher  practise a six-action sequence and get feedback from the teacher.  display a six-action sequence and get feedback from the teacher and peers.  discuss the safety precautions to be when performing a two and three partner balances
strands.inquiryQuestions: How is a sequence useful in life?

strands.outcomes: By the end of the Sub Strand, the learner should be able to: a) define the term speed as used in Physical and Health Education. b) identify physical activities that can be used to develop speed. c) perform physical fitness exercises for developing speed to enhance the ‘spirit of sports value’ Health d) observe precautions when perform physical fitness exercises for developing speed e) appreciate developing speed for everyday chores.
strands.experiences: The learner is guided individually, in pairs or in groups to:  use the library, digital devices or other sources of information to find out the meaning of speed.  discuss and come up with physical activities that can be used to develop speed.  discuss the precautions that need to be observed when performing physical fitness exercises for developing speed  practice the physical activities that can be used to develop speed. and give each other feedback.
strands.inquiryQuestions: How is speed related to your overall wellbeing?

strands.outcomes: By the end of the Sub Strand, the learner should be able to: a) define the term power as used in Physical and Health Education b) identify physical activities that can be used to develop power c) perform physical activities for developing power to enhance the competence of self-efficacy d) appreciate power in everyday activities.
strands.experiences: The learner is guided individually or in groups to:  use the library, digital devices or other sources of information to find out the meaning of power.  discuss physical activities that can be used to develop power.  practise physical activities that develop reaction time and observe safety.
strands.inquiryQuestions: Why is power important in everyday life?

strands.outcomes: By the end of the Sub-Strand, the learner should be able to: a) define the term coordination as used in Physical and Health Education. b) identify physical activities that can be used to develop coordination. c) practise coordination to enhance the ‘spirit of sports value’ Health for healthy living. d) appreciate coordination in everyday life.
strands.experiences: The learner is guided individually or in groups to:  use the library, digital devices or other sources of information to find out the meaning of power.  discuss physical activities that can be used to develop coordination.  practise physical activities that develop coordination and observe safety.
strands.inquiryQuestions: Why is power important in everyday life?

strands.outcomes: By the end of the Sub Strand, the learner should be able to: a) define the term leadership styles as used in Physical and Health Education b) delegate activities to the team during outdoor activities c) outline the characteristics of each style of leadership to enhance self-management skills d) play games for fun and enjoyment during outdoor activities e) embrace different leadership styles for good leadership
strands.experiences: The learner is guided individually, in pairs or in groups to:  use the dictionary, library, digital devices and other sources of information to search for the meaning of the term leadership styles.  use digital devices and other sources of information to find out the characteristics of each style of leadership and write down.  discuss the type of games that are appropriate to play during an outdoor activity
strands.inquiryQuestions: Why are leaders important in a community?

strands.subStrand: Outdoor Activities: Lighting the Camp fire 3 Lessons
strands.outcomes: By the end of the Sub Strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify appropriate materials for use in lighting fire during an outdoor activity b) perform laying wood in readiness for a campfire c) lighting a campfire during an outdoor activity d) observe precautions when lighting a fire camp fire for fire safety e) managing a campfire during an outdoor activity to enhance ‘Spirit of Sports Value ‘Community and solidarity
strands.experiences: The learner is guided individually, in pairs or in groups to:  discuss and write down the most appropriate materials that can be used to light a camp fire  practise laying wood in readiness for a camp fire during an outdoor activity  discuss the necessary precautions to be observed when lighting a camp fire during an outdoor activity  in pairs assist one another to light a camp fire  discuss how to managing a campfire during an outdoor activity
strands.inquiryQuestions: 1. How can materials for lighting fire be used and reused during outdoor activity? 2. How can waste be managed during an outdoor activity?

strands.subStrand: Outdoor Activities: Choosing and constructing shelter. 5 Lessons (project)
strands.outcomes: By the end of the Sub Strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify a suitable site for setting up shelter in the local environment. b) state appropriate locally available materials that can be used to set up shelter during an outdoor activity c) observe precautions for own and others safety when setting up shelter.
strands.experiences: The learner is guided individually, in pars or in groups to:  explore the local environment to identify a suitable a site for setting up shelter.  discuss the most appropriate locally available materials for setting up shelter.  discuss the precautionary measures that need to be observed when setting up shelter during an outdoor activity
strands.inquiryQuestions: Why is it important to use locally available material when setting up shelter?

strands.outcomes: By the end of the Sub Strand, the learner should be able to: a) explain the causes of fainting to develop the competence of Learning to learn b) identify the signs and symptoms of fainting for appropriate management c) observes safety precautions when performing the first aid procedure for fainting d) practise the first aid procedure for fainting e) appreciate first aid in assisting to save life.
strands.experiences: The learner is guided individually, in pairs or in groups to:  use the library, the internet and other sources of information to find out the causes of fainting and write down.  use the library, the internet and other sources of information to write down the signs and symptoms of fainting  use digital devices to watch video clips on the first aid procedure for fainting.  Discuss the precautions that need to be observed when attending to a person who has fainted  practise the first aid procedure for fainting and get feedback from the teacher.
strands.inquiryQuestions: Why is it important to manage fainting appropriately?

strands.subStrand: Sports related injuries: Insects bites and stings 2 Lessons
strands.outcomes: By the end of the Sub-Strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify signs and symptoms of insect’s bites and stings for appropriate management b) identify traditional ways of treating insects’ bites and stings c) state the first aid procedure for insect’s bites and stings d) perform first aid procedures for insect’s bites and stings appreciate first aid on insect’s bites and stings to alleviate pain.
strands.experiences: The learner is guided individually, in pairs or in groups to:  discuss and identify the types of insets found in your locality and list those that bite and sting.  discuss in groups the signs and symptoms of insect’s bites and stings and write down.  use digital devices to view videos on first aid procedures applied on and insects’ bites and stings.  discuss the traditional ways of treating insects’ bites and stings. practise the Fist Aid procedures for insects’ bites and stings and get feedback from the teacher.
strands.inquiryQuestions: 1. Which type of insects are found in the school compound? 2. Which insect bites and stings are common in the community?

strands.subStrand: Sports related injuries: Snake bite. 3 Lessons
strands.outcomes: By the end of the Sub Strand, the learner should be able to: a) identify signs and symptoms of a snake bite. b) state the first aid procedures and management for a snake bite. c) practise the first aid procedures for snake bites. d) appreciate first aid on snake bites for saving life.
strands.experiences: The learner is guided individually, in pairs or in groups to:  discuss the type and names of snakes found in your community.  use the digital media and other sources of information to identify signs and symptoms of snake bites from your community.  use the digital media and other sources of information to discuss the first aid procedures and management for snake bites.  practise the Fist Aid procedures and management for snake bites.
strands.inquiryQuestions: Why is First Aid for a snake bite victim important?

strands.subStrand: Sports related injuries: Bandages and Dressings. 7 Lessons
strands.outcomes: By the end of the Sub Strand, the learner should be able to: a) define the terms bandages and dressings as used in First Aid b) identify the different types of bandages and dressings in first aid c) describe the triangular bandage in First Aid. d) state the many ways a triangular bandage can be off in First Aid e) identify suitable materials for making a triangular bandage f) make a triangular Bandage for use in First Aid. g) embrace making a triangular bandage for use in First Aid.
strands.experiences: The learner is guided individually, in pairs or in groups to:  use the digital devices to check for the definition of the term’s bandages and dressings in First Aid.  discuss and write down the types of bandages and dressings in First Aid.  use digital devices, pictures and photographs to observe a triangular bandage.  discuss how to use a triangular bandage for first aid  identify suitable materials for making a triangular bandage.  discuss the most appropriate material for making a suitable material for making a triangular bandage  make a triangular Bandage fand practice using it with a partner
strands.inquiryQuestions: Why is preparing bandages and dressing in advance important?

strands.subStrand: Sports related injuries: Slings and splints 5 Lessons
strands.outcomes: By the end of the Sub Strand, the learner should be able to: a) define a sling and a splint as used in First Aid b) state the functions of a sling and a splint in First Aid c) tie the reef knot on a triangular bandage to secure it d) use the triangular bandage to practise slinging an injured arm in First Aid.
strands.experiences: The learner is guided individually, in pairs or in groups to:  use the internet to assist in defining the terms sling and splint as used in First Aid and write down.  discuss the functions of a sling and a splint and write down.  demonstrate how to tie the reef knot on a triangular bandage and get feedback from the teacher.  demonstrate how to use the triangular bandage in slinging an injured arm and get feedback from the teacher.  practise slinging an injured arm and give each other feedback.
strands.inquiryQuestions: Why is a reef knot used in tying knots on slings in first aid?

strands.subStrand: Sports related injuries. Two and four- handed seat. 3 Lessons
strands.outcomes: By the end of the Sub Strand, the learner should be able to: a) explain the Two and Four- handed seat carry method for an injured person. b) practise the Two and Four- handed seat carry method for an injured person. c) embrace the Two and Four-handed seat carry method for an injured person.
strands.experiences: The learner is guided individually, in pairs or in groups to:  use the digital devices to watch video clips on the Two and Four- handed seat carry method and observe the hand formation.  demonstrate the Two and Four- handed seat carry method and get feedback from the teacher  practise the Two and Four-handed seat carry method and give each other feedback.
strands.inquiryQuestions: What instance are the Two and Four-handed seat carry method applicable?

strands.subStrand: Sports related injuries: Bone fractures and dislocation 5 Lessons
strands.outcomes: By the end of the Sub Strand, the learner should be able to: a) define the term bone fracture and dislocation as used in First Aid b) identify types of bone fractures for appropriate management c) state the difference between bone fractures and dislocation in First Aid d) use the human skeleton to identify areas where dislocations occur e) use a triangular bandage to splint a broken arm.
strands.experiences: The learner is guided individually, in pairs or in groups to:  use digital devices to assist in defining the term bone fracture and dislocation as used in first aid.  use the digital devices to identify types of bone fractures.  use digital devices to find out the difference between bone fracture and dislocation in First Aid.  use digital devices or provided images of human skeleton to identify areas where dislocations occur.  use digital devices to describe the signs and symptoms of a bone fracture and dislocation.  demonstrate how to use locally available materials (newspaper, piece of a plastic container, and wood plank) to splint and sling an injured arm using the triangular bandage.
strands.inquiryQuestions: Why is splinting a broken arm important as the injured person is transported to hospital?
